title: LoL Esports |
content:
Welcome to theLCS Homegrounds: Mexico City Showdownhosted by LYON, where four of the league's biggest teams will battle it out live during Week 6 of the LCS on August 29-30.

Hosted by LYON, the event will feature LYON, Cloud9, Team Liquid, and Shopify Rebellion competing in front of a live crowd at Arena Esports Stadium at CINEMEX Artz Pedregal in Mexico City, the same venue where DRX began their miracle run at Worlds 2022.

This is the first team homegrounds initiative for the LCS, and we are eager to work with LYON for this debut event. Homegrounds is all about bringing the LCS closer to fans across the Americas, creating unforgettable live experiences in the home markets that make our community so special. We will be watching fan feedback to take into potential future homegrounds opportunities, so let us know what you think!

Tickets will be available soon, so be sure to keep an eye on LYON's social media channels for on-sale information. We can't wait to see you in Mexico City!

title: League of Legends World Championship tickets are appearing for over $3,000, but Riot may not be the one to blame
summary: League of Legends World Championship tickets are appearing for over $3,000, but Riot may not be the one to blame  Esports Insider
content:
Olivia Richman is a seasoned esports journalist who has worked with Inven Global, Esports Illustrated, Esports.gg, and more. As an editor and writer at Esports Insider, she loves telling unique esports stories, especially within the FGC. When not working and gaming, Olivia loves collecting Kirby plush, eating sushi, and driving her cars at the track.

The esports community is raging after the2026 League of Legends World Championshipfinals tickets went on sale. Passionate fans set their alarm, verified their account through three different two-factor apps, waited in a digital queue with thousands of other people… Then saw almost every seat vanish in 30 seconds.

As you may have guessed by now, those ticketspopped up on resale sites, marked up by roughly 300%. The scalping crisis in competitive gaming has reached a boiling point, but it goes far beyond esports. It’s a complex situation that’s under legal scrutiny after multiple safeguards failed to deliver the tickets to esports fans.

And you may be placing the blame on the wrong entity.

When general admission tickets dropped for the 2026 League of Legends World Championship final at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, the entire inventory seemed to disappear instantly. The Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York hasseating for 19,000 people. That seems pretty large, but the Chengdu Dong’an Lake Sports Park Arena, which had 18,000 seats, sold out last year.

A lot of these seats, however, apparently went to partners, sponsors, and… Blech,influencers. We all know how muchesports fans love that. According toConcert Informant, 3,200 tickets went to the Fan First pre-sale and 1,100 went to influencers (among other entities), but this has not been verified. Even if this were true, there would still be about half the venue left. Despite this, Riot apparently only dropped 430 tickets on Ticketmaster.
